transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the August 25 production policy review for the public API rate-limit project, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers, but per our normal review process, I need backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations to report your release-impacting findings before I record the final policy. The current draft has 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, the same limit applied to authentication endpoints, and no specified staffed launch window. I'd like to hear from each of you on any concerns or findings you have so we can get this wrapped up properly.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a release-impacting finding from backend engineering. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our backend load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. The current draft limit of 100 requests per minute would break legitimate bulk-import synchronization. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this needs to be addressed before the final policy is recorded.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered this clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this contractual notice requirement needs to be factored into the final policy and its rollout timing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which would be insufficient to protect against credential abuse. This finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but it needs to be addressed before the final policy is recorded.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from support operations. Support Operations confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I have not added the coverage block to the launch plan because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated. This means our staffed launch window is constrained to that two-hour block on September 15, which is relevant for finalizing the rollout timing and policy.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Update the ordinary API-key limit to 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window per backend engineering's load replay findings.
Apply a separate limit of 30 requests per minute per API key to authentication endpoints per security's credential-abuse investigation findings.
Send contractual notice to Acme on September 1 so enforcement can begin on September 15, satisfying the 14-day notice requirement.
Schedule the staffed launch during the 10:00 to 12:00 UTC window on September 15 with the documented escalation handoff.
